MARKING SCHEME:
 HISTORY & GOVERNMENT FORM 4
 MID-TERM 2 EXAM 2026
 SECTION A (25 MARKS)
 1. Relationship between History and Government:
 History is the study of past events, while Government is the study of how people are
 governed; History provides the background/context upon which modern government
 systems are built. (1mk)
 2. Tools of Middle Stone Age:
 Sangoan tools, Tangue tools, Scrapers, Flake tools. (Any 2 x 1 = 2mks)
 3. Agriculture in Egypt:
 Presence of the River Nile which provided water for irrigation and fertile silt during
 flooding. (1mk)
 4. Metals in Pre-colonial Africa:
 Iron, Gold, Copper, Bronze. (Any 2 x 1 = 2mks)
 5. Disadvantages of bird messaging:
 They could be preyed upon/killed; they could get lost; they could only carry limited/short
 messages; affected by weather. (Any 2 x 1 = 2mks)
 6. Advantage of steam engine:
 It provided a faster and more reliable source of power that could carry heavier loads than
 animal power. (1mk)
 7. Medical discoveries (19th Century):
 Chloroform (Anesthesia) by James Simpson; Penicillin by Alexander Fleming; Germ theory
 by Louis Pasteur; Antiseptic surgery by Joseph Lister. (Any 2 x 1 = 2mks)
 8. Growth of Meroe:
 Availability of iron ore/growth of iron working industry; strategic location at the junction of
 trade routes. (1mk)
 9. Head of Shona:
 Mwenemutapa (Mwene Mutapa). (1mk)
 10. Methods of acquiring colonies:
 Treaty making/signing; Use of force/Military conquest; Treachery/Deception; Company
 rule. (Any 2 x 1 = 2mks)
 11. Why Indirect Rule in N. Nigeria:
 Lack of enough British personnel; to reduce the cost of administration; existence of an
 organized system of government (Sokoto Caliphate). (1mk)
 12. Functions of ICJ:
 Settling legal disputes submitted by states; giving advisory opinions on legal questions
 referred by international organs. (Any 2 x 1 = 2mks)
 13. Triple Entente Leader:
 Britain (King George V) / France (Raymond Poincaré). (1mk)
 14. Failure of League of Nations:
 Lack of its own military/army; The USA refused to join; Lack of financial resources; Member
 states concerned with national interests. (Any 2 x 1 = 2mks)
 15. UN promoting human rights:
 Through the Universal Declaration of Human Rights; sending observers to monitor
 elections; sanctioning countries that violate rights. (1mk)
 16. ANC Military Wing:
 Umkhonto we Sizwe (Spear of the Nation). (1mk)
 17. Function of US Executive:
 To implement/enforce federal laws; to formulate foreign policy. (1mk)
 SECTION B (45 MARKS)
 Question 18
 (a) Invention of the Wheel (3 marks)
 • • Facilitated movement of heavy loads.
 • Led to development of animal-drawn carts.
 • Improved speed of travel on land.
 (b) Factors for Agrarian Revolution in Britain (12 marks)
 • • Enclosure system: Consolidated small land fragments into large farms.
 • Mechanization: Seed drill and horse-drawn hoe.
 • Selective Breeding: Robert Bakewell (superior livestock).
 • Crop Rotation: Norfolk four-course system (turnips, clover, wheat, barley).
 • Fertilizers: Use of manure and chemical fertilizers.
 • Infrastructure: Improved roads and railways to reach urban markets.
 Question 20
 (b) Consequences of the Partition of Africa (12 marks)
 • • Loss of Independence: African states lost sovereignty.
 • Language and Culture: Introduction of European languages.
 • Boundary Disputes: Arbitrary borders split ethnic groups.
 • Religion: Spread of Christianity.
 • Infrastructure: Railways/roads built for extraction of materials.
 • Exploitation: Forced labor, heavy taxation, and loss of fertile land.
 SECTION C (30 MARKS)
 Question 22
 (b) Effects of World War II (12 marks)
 • • Rise of Superpowers: USA and USSR dominant.
 • Formation of the UN: To prevent future global conflicts.
 • Decolonization: Accelerated movement for independence in Africa/Asia.
 • Massive Destruction: Immense loss of human life and infrastructure.
 • Economic Impact: Marshall Plan for rebuilding Europe.
 • Social Changes: Focus on human rights and women in workforce.
 Question 24
 (b) Functions of the US President (12 marks)
 • • Head of State: Ceremonial duties and international representation.
 • Chief Executive: Implementation of federal laws.
 • Commander-in-Chief: Head of the US Armed Forces.
 • Legislative Role: Veto power and State of the Union address.
 • Diplomatic Role: Negotiating treaties.
 • Appointing Authority: Nominates federal judges and cabinet members.
